newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening mixed, PGMs lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening mixed, PGMs lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening mixed Wednesday, with gold and silver seen firmer, but platinum group metals (PGMs) expected to continue their retreat.
In overnight news the Japanese trade surplus for May surged more than 200 pct over the May 1996 surplus, putting pressure on the U.S. dollar which helped gold in the bullion market.
While the revised European Union treaty signed Monday, suggested that longer term the new euro currency may not be a strong one which may also help gold, traders said.
On a negative note though, the Swiss parliament approved a revised charter for the Swiss central bank, allowing it to start lending gold to improve its earnings.
The charter also reduced the amount of gold the Swiss National Bank must hold to cover its notes in circulation to 25 percent from 40 percent.
COMEX August gold was seen opening unchanged to up 50 cents an ounce from Tuesday's close at $343.70 an ounce.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $342.20/50 early, compared to the London Wednesday morning fix at $342.05 and the New York close Tuesday around $341.50/00.
COMEX gold stocks slipped 32 ounces to 828,887 ounces Tuesday, while COMEX silver stocks fell a further 2,986,381 ounces to 185,003,689 ounces, the lowest level in several months.
COMEX July silver was seen opening unchanged to up 0.5 cent an ounce from Tuesday's close at $4.762.

NYMEX July platinum was seen opening down $2.00 to $3.00 an ounce from the previous close at $411.10, while NYMEX September palladium was seen opening down $2.00 to $3.00 an ounce from Tuesday's close at $177.90.

In overnight news, the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said it was in discussions with the London Platinum and Palladium Market Association about restoring orderly trading conditions to the PGM market.

A senior TOCOM official also said TOCOM would introduce position limits for platinum futures of 600 lots per individual investor in the spot month. Positions in the second delivery month would be limited to 1200 lots.
